title: Seizures (Fits)
summary: Protect them from injury, time the seizure, and do not hold them down or put anything in their mouth. Recovery position once the jerking stops.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} if any of these apply
when: The seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, or another starts soon after
It is their first seizure, or you don't know their history
They are injured, in water, pregnant or diabetic
They have trouble breathing or don't wake up after the seizure

steps.title: Note the time it started
steps.text: Timing helps decide when to call for help and helps doctors.

steps.title: Protect them
steps.text: Move hard or sharp objects away. Cushion their head with something soft. Loosen tight clothing around the neck. Remove glasses.

steps.title: Let the seizure run its course
steps.text: Stay with them and observe. Note what happens so you can tell responders.

steps.title: When the jerking stops
steps.text: Check breathing and place them in the recovery position. Stay with them until they are fully awake. Talk calmly – they may be confused.

steps.title: If they are not breathing normally
Emergency seizure medicine
steps.text: If they have a prescribed emergency seizure medicine and a care plan, help them use it as directed by the plan.

doNot: Do not restrain or hold them down
Do not put anything in their mouth
Do not move them unless they are in danger
Do not give food or drink until they are fully alert

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
